title: Pixel Loom
tagline: A little world, one pixel at a time.
description: A local-first pixel-art and flipbook editor. Draw on transparent layers, animate small sprites, and export PNG frames or sprite sheets.
projectNotes: Inspired by Aseprite’s pixel-art and animation workflow. This is an independent learning project, not an official Aseprite app or a claim of feature-for-feature compatibility.
Editable projects use Pixel Loom’s own JSON format. Aseprite project files, GIF/APNG export, selections, and variable frame timing are not supported.
Create canvases up to 128 × 128 pixels with up to 12 layers and 32 frames, within a total limit of two million stored cells.
Artwork stays in your browser. Download editable project backups for important work; browser autosave is best effort and can be lost if storage is cleared.

title: Kata Pulse Foundry
tagline: Four voices. Sixteen steps. Your next little obsession.
description: A small, local-first drum sequencer. Build a four-voice loop, adjust its tempo, and save a WAV or editable project.
features: Two starter loops and a blank loop
projectNotes: Inspired by FL Studio’s step-sequencing workflow. This is an independent learning project, not an official FL Studio app or a claim of full feature compatibility.
This first version is a four-voice, 16-step drum sequencer. It does not include a piano roll, arrangement timeline, recording, plugins, MIDI, or FLP project support.
WAV exports contain one bar plus a 0.6-second sound tail, rather than a seamless looping WAV. Editable projects use this app’s own JSON format.
Loops stay in your browser. Local autosave is best effort; download project backups for important work. Physical phones and hardware listening have not been tested.

title: Trackstead
tagline: A place for sound to take shape.
description: A local-first multitrack audio sketchbook: arrange, trim and split clips, balance tracks, capture an opt-in mic take, save projects, and export stereo WAV.
features: Clip trim, split, duplicate, and fades
Per-track gain, pan, mute, and solo
projectNotes: Inspired by REAPER’s linear, nondestructive multitrack workflow, with an original interface and demo audio. This independent learning project is not affiliated with Cockos or REAPER.
Arrange up to 12 tracks, 120 clips, and five minutes of audio. There is no MIDI, plugin hosting, time stretching, live input monitoring, or REAPER .rpp project compatibility.

Microphone recording is opt-in and has not been tested with real microphone hardware. Mobile/touch interaction and cross-browser behavior remain unverified; this prototype is intended for desktop use.
Save your project before closing or reloading: Trackstead has no autosave. Projects embed audio in the app’s own format. Audio stays in your browser.

title: Kata Mosslight
description: A quiet digital painting studio with expressive brushes, real paint layers, and a meadow waiting for your first mark.
features: Eight raster layers with opacity and blend modes
Layer reorder, rename, duplicate and clear
projectNotes: Inspired by Krita’s digital-painting workflow. This independent learning project uses original interface artwork and a layered meadow study; it is not an official Krita app or a claim of full feature compatibility.
This first version uses a fixed 1200 × 900 canvas and up to eight raster layers. It does not support Krita .kra or PSD files, animation, masks, transforms, or physical pigment simulation.

Pen pressure is supported where the browser provides it, but physical pen, pressure, and touch hardware have not been tested. The narrow capture shows a 390 × 844 iframe viewport, not a physical phone.
Paintings stay in your browser. Autosave uses one local slot shared by tabs and depends on browser storage. Keep editable project downloads as backups; PNG exports flatten the layers.
